correctness.rationale: In the source model the exactly observed total recovered variable \(C=R+R_\infty Q\) satisfies \(\dot C=\gamma I\). Division by \(\dot P\) and integration gives the scalar \(F_k\) identity. The elasticity \(\eta(z)=z/[(1+z^2)\arctan z]\) has strictly negative derivative \(\big[(1-z^2)\arctan z-z\big]/\big[(1+z^2)^2(\arctan z)^2\big]\). Weighted averages over two disjoint intervals prove the ratio \(\Phi\) strictly increasing. Uniform endpoint limits give strict sharp bounds, and the inversion formula yields unique positive \(\alpha,\rho\) for the reduced observation relation. The standard-library checker and full-ODE numerical integration corroborate computations but are not relied upon for proof.

value.rationale: Exact finite-data identification and a parameter-free sharp model-falsification interval resolve a natural inference gap created by the original paper's numerical fitting of \(\rho\) and \(\alpha\). The result isolates mobility scale from intensity without observing prevalence or fitting \(\beta\) and \(\beta_R\), and reveals extreme-saturation weak sensitivity. Its motivated object and precise invariant are relevant to spatial outbreak inference and cannot be obtained merely by rerunning a known table.
